implementation_statement: No security policy existed before 2026. POL-02 (access control, with program governance and workforce use rules) was approved by the Principal on 2026-09-18 and takes effect 2026-10-01. A one-page account procedure (onboarding, offboarding, guest accounts) is due 2026-10-31.

The Office Manager creates staff and guest accounts in SYS-02, which provides single sign-on to SYS-01, SYS-03, SYS-04, and SYS-06. Gaps: no offboarding checklist; the 9 subsidiary guest accounts were never reviewed and a former Marine Supply controller kept access from February to 2026-08-14; the MSP uses one shared global administrator account.
evidence: SYS-02 user and guest export (2026-08-05); MSP admin account record

implementation_statement: SYS-07 enforces per-family-member folders, and family members see only their own. Gap: in SYS-02 the Family site grants all 7 staff access to every family folder, including tax returns, estate plans, and medical bills.
evidence: SYS-02 site permission report; SYS-07 folder permission report

implementation_statement: Banks enforce dual approval for wires and ACH batches on every office, family entity, and subsidiary account. Gap: the bill pay platform (SYS-03) lets the Senior Accountant change payee bank details and release payments alone (P07 finding, 2026-09-01).
evidence: Bank entitlement reports; SYS-03 role settings

implementation_statement: Staff have no local administrator rights on laptops (MSP policy). Gaps: two standing global administrators in SYS-02 (the Office Manager and the MSP shared account); the Family site is open to all staff; the AI assistant inherits that over-broad access.
evidence: MSP endpoint policy; SYS-02 admin role report

implementation_statement: SYS-01 to SYS-04, SYS-06, and SYS-07 lock accounts after repeated failed sign-ins using vendor defaults (confirmed in settings).
The MSP enforces a 10-minute screen lock on all 8 laptops; the conference-room PC uses a kiosk account with no file access (since 2026-08-21).

Staff reach SaaS systems over the internet with MFA; there is no VPN. The MSP reaches laptops through its remote management tool. Gaps: SYS-11's remote desktop port is open to the internet (office IP allowlist only, local password); the office has no evidence of how the MSP protects its remote tool.
evidence: Cloud firewall rule export for SYS-11; MSP questionnaire (pending)

implementation_statement: Gap: staff read email and approve MFA prompts on personal phones with no mobile management. Planned: app protection policy for email and files (PIN, no saving to the phone, remote wipe of office data) by 2026-11-30.
Staff watch a yearly security awareness video (since 2024). Gaps: no content on the office's own risks (payment fraud, family privacy), no phishing exercises, no record of who completed it in 2025.

Gap: no training on recognizing and reporting social engineering, although email payment fraud is the office's top risk. Planned: payment-fraud module and quarterly simulations for all staff, plus a family briefing, from 2026-10.

provider_if_inherited: Productivity suite vendor; SaaS vendors; MSP
implementation_statement: SYS-02 records sign-ins, mailbox, and file activity at the license default. SaaS vendors log their own events. The MSP keeps firewall logs. Gap: the events that matter (inbox rule creation, forwarding, mass download, admin changes) are not defined or alerted.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: nobody reviews sign-in, mailbox, or admin logs. Planned: monthly review by the Family Office Director with a checklist, plus MSP-routed alerts (SI-4), from 2026-11.
Logs are kept for the SYS-02 license default, which is shorter than one year. Planned: license upgrade with one-year audit log retention by 2026-12-31.
An independent consultant assessed 13 controls on 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-02 (P07). The office will repeat an independent assessment each year.
The MSP keeps a list of the 8 laptops, the conference PC, and the printer. Gaps: no list of SaaS systems and service providers, and no inventory of where family personal information is stored.
The BIA (P05) was approved 2026-09-18. Gap: no contingency plan. Planned: a short plan with recovery steps, backup bank approvers, and the storm checklist by 2026-12-31.
Gap: no restore of any system has ever been tested. Planned: first SYS-11 snapshot restore by 2026-10-31 and quarterly restore tests of the new SYS-02 backup.

SaaS vendors back up their own platforms. SYS-11 has daily snapshots kept 14 days in the same cloud account. Gaps: no independent backup of SYS-02 mail and files; SYS-11 snapshots can be deleted with the same MSP credentials that run the server.
evidence: Cloud snapshot policy export; vendor documentation

implementation_statement: Each staff member has a named account and signs in once through SYS-02. Gap: the MSP's global administrator account is shared among technicians.

Administrator accounts use authenticator push MFA. Gaps: the MSP shared admin account's MFA is registered to the MSP help desk phone; SYS-11 local administrator sign-in over remote desktop uses a password only; push MFA has no number matching and can be phished.
evidence: SYS-02 MFA registration report; SYS-11 access test (P07)

implementation_statement: All staff and guests must use MFA (authenticator push) in SYS-02; banks and custodians use hardware tokens. Upgrade to phishing-resistant security keys planned by 2026-12-31 (P01 R-001).
Passwords are at least 12 characters in SYS-02. Gaps: no password manager; the staff Wi-Fi password has not changed since 2023; one family member shared a vault password until 2026-08-20.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy approved 2026-09-18, effective 2026-10-01.
Gap: no incident handling process. Planned: the P08 runbook (approved 2026-09-18) and a tabletop with the MSP by 2026-11-30.

Staff tell the Family Office Director about problems informally. Gaps: no reporting deadline and no log; the March 2026 payment fraud attempt was never recorded. POL-03 sets a 1-hour reporting rule from 2026-10-01.
Gap: no incident response plan before 2026. The P08 runbook is the plan for the office's most likely serious incident; printed copies and a contact card are due 2026-10-15.

Paper goes to a locked shredding bin emptied monthly by a shredding service. The MSP wipes laptops before reuse. Gap: no record of electronic disposal and no disposal of records past a retention date.
evidence: Shredding service receipts; MSP ticket history

implementation_statement: Keyed suite entry with an after-hours alarm; keys held by the Office Manager, Family Office Director, and Controller; locked file room; bank tokens and original documents kept in a safe.
This SSP was approved by the Principal on 2026-09-18 and will be reviewed each year with the risk assessment.
Workforce use rules are in POL-02 Part C (approved 2026-09-18), including the approved AI tools rule. Gap: signed acknowledgments not yet collected (due 2026-10-31).

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The Principal designated the Family Office Director as Qualified Individual and security lead in writing on 2026-08-14.

When an employee leaves, the Office Manager disables the SYS-02 account (which ends single sign-on) on request. Gaps: no checklist, no deadline, no step for bank tokens, the vault, or guest accounts of subsidiary staff who leave.
Gap: the office does not know which MSP technicians can reach its systems or what security duties bind them. Planned: technician list and security terms in the MSP contract amendment by 2026-12-31.
The first risk assessment was completed 2026-08-14 with NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01) and will be updated every August and after major changes.

Gap: no vulnerability scanning. Planned: MSP monthly external and internal scans (including SYS-11) from 2026-11. The office has fewer than 5,000 consumers, so the specific scanning and penetration testing schedule in 314.4(d)(2) does not apply; 314.4(d)(1) still requires regular testing or monitoring.

Vendors are chosen on business grounds. SOC 2 Type 2 reports were received from the accounting system and investment platform vendors. Gaps: no list of service providers with access to family information; the reports were never reviewed; the MSP contract has no security terms.
The office firewall blocks unsolicited inbound traffic and separates guest Wi-Fi. Gap: SYS-11 accepts remote desktop connections from the internet (IP allowlist).
evidence: Firewall rule export; cloud firewall rule export

implementation_statement: All SaaS, bank, and custodian connections use TLS. Family documents go to the CPA firm and counsel by vault share links, not email attachments.
SaaS vendors encrypt stored data; the MSP encrypts all laptops; SYS-11 disks use the provider's default encryption. Gap: personal phones that hold email are not managed or confirmed encrypted.
The MSP patches laptops automatically and SYS-11 monthly. Gaps: SYS-11's operating system reaches end of vendor support in October 2026; the printer was outside patching until 2026-08-21.
MSP-managed antivirus on all laptops and SYS-11, with alerts to the MSP during business hours; SYS-02 scans email attachments and links.

Gap: no monitoring beyond antivirus. Planned: MSP-managed endpoint detection and response with after-hours alerting, and SYS-02 alerts for risky sign-ins, new inbox rules, forwarding, and mass download, by 2026-12-31.

Gap: no retention schedule; family tax returns and IDs since 2009 and former household employees' forms are kept indefinitely. Planned: retention schedule approved by counsel and the CPA firm, then disposal, by 2027-03-31.
